records.summary: Bitquery's 19 October XRPL RLUSD investigation reports that 99.6% of the sampled RLUSD payment count came from a 110-wallet dust cluster carrying only 7,722 RLUSD. The cluster's Binance-labelled funding wallet rDAE53 is the exact same address as one of the five Binance-labelled XRP incident sources. Bithomp confirms that rDAE53 later sent 11.141M XRP and 51.173M RLUSD to another Binance-labelled account after the 185.017M XRP transfer. Bithomp body balances for the five source accounts imply 45.99 XRP combined, but page title/body fields disagree by 7 XRP in aggregate. The $7.33B high-value RLUSD gross flow includes issuer plumbing and a matched roundtrip; no net-capital or XRP-demand conclusion is admitted.
actions: Opened Bitquery's complete RLUSD XRPL investigation and preserved its exact sample window, payment definitions, bot-cluster methodology, high-value transfer decomposition, and explicit attribution limitations.
Matched rDAE53 exactly across the RLUSD bot-funding investigation and the 185,017,485.5 XRP incident transfer; retained the distinction between common address and common operator.
Inspected current Bithomp pages for all five source accounts and the rs8Z destination; recorded body/title balance discrepancies rather than claiming raw account_info verification.
Verified two post-incident successful payments from rDAE53 to rs8Z: 11,141,435.843 XRP at 23:12:20 UTC on 29 October and 51,172,508 RLUSD at 01:27:10 UTC on 30 October.
Decomposed RLUSD gross volume into issuer mint/redemption and a matched roundtrip; recorded the residual net-capital unknown.
Audited current main, open PRs, CI runs and the task-bundle quality-gate issue.
Updated PR #1385 with a deterministic guard against destructive workspace rollback commands and 12 local regex cases.

Identified that the XRP ledger validation workflow ran isolated fixture tests but did not invoke the repository validator; added the actual validator step and a regression test on the research PR branch.
blockers: Bitquery's RLUSD bot analysis is a single-provider attribution; beneficial owners remain unknown.
The exact rDAE53 address match does not connect the bot operator to the XRP theft actor.
Bithomp account title/body balances conflict; raw validated account_info is not yet available.
Official Binance October 1 XRP PoR address export has not been downloaded and cross-matched.
The attacker receiver has not been refreshed after the previously captured 06:43 UTC cutoff.
The new actual-repository validation workflow step is pending exact-head CI.
PR #1385's new destructive-rollback guard is pending exact-head CI.
Full repository CI, dependency audit and vulnerability scan remain unrun.
next_actions: Run the new exact-head research workflow and verify the actual repository validator returns PASS with 282 archive shards and 11 source references.
Obtain raw account_info for all five source accounts and rs8Z, then reconcile Bithomp page balances.
Crosswalk all five source accounts and rs8Z against Binance's official PoR export.
Refresh the attacker receiver and track subsequent transactions.
Construct actual-capital features from distinct beneficial owners, net external flows, issuer flows, matched roundtrips and exchange/custody omnibus classifications.
Keep the XRP prediction engine in shadow mode; no forecast until fixed-horizon, leakage-safe out-of-sample validation and calibration are executed.
